headline: Record sales, GAAP EPS dips on deal costs, guidance raised
summary_short: Eaton reported record Q2 2026 sales of $8,531M (+21.4% y/y) on 14% organic growth above guidance, while GAAP diluted EPS fell to $2.11 (-15.9% y/y) on deal and amortization charges even as adjusted EPS hit a Q2 record $3.15 (+6.8% y/y).
summary_long: Sales rose to a record $8,531M on 14% organic growth plus 7% from acquisitions (Boyd Thermal, Ultra PCS, Fibrebond, Resilient). Segment margins of 23.1% beat the high end of guidance but were down 80bp y/y; Electrical Americas margins rose 190bp sequentially to 27.5%. GAAP diluted EPS fell 15.9% y/y to $2.11 on $0.49/share acquisition-and-divestiture charges, $0.05/share restructuring, and $0.50/share intangible amortization; adjusted EPS rose 6.8% y/y to a Q2 record $3.15. Interest expense nearly tripled to $201M and long-term debt rose 87.4% y/y to $18,520M on acquisition financing. Free cash flow was $874M, up 22% y/y. Eaton raised full-year organic-growth and adjusted-EPS guidance and disclosed an agreement to separate its Mobility segment with Dana.

drivers.explanation: CEO Paulo Ruiz attributed the quarter to accelerated momentum, record sales and solid earnings from strong organic growth, disciplined execution driving sequential margin expansion (especially Electrical Americas), and robust demand across end markets including data centers, prompting raised full-year organic-growth guidance.

The sales increase consisted of 14% organic sales growth and 7% growth from acquisitions; Electrical Global alone grew 44%, including a 25-point contribution from Boyd Thermal in its first full quarter post-acquisition.

Cost of products sold rose faster than revenue (+28.1% vs +21.4% y/y), consistent with the release's reported 80bp y/y segment-margin decline to 23.1% and higher acquisition-related integration costs embedded in cost of sales.
Gross profit dollars grew on higher volume, but gross margin compressed to 33.5% from 37.0% y/y since cost of products sold outpaced revenue growth; not itself a labeled release metric.
Total segment operating profit rose 17.4% y/y to $1,974M, led by Electrical Global (+41%) and Electrical Americas (+10%), per the disclosed segment table.
Tracks the segment operating-profit growth above, net of higher Corporate items (intangible amortization, restructuring) disclosed in the segment reconciliation.

Follows the operating-profit increase plus a higher depreciation and amortization addback, consistent with the sharp rise in intangible asset amortization ($255M vs $129M y/y) tied to recent acquisitions.

Despite segment operating-profit growth, pretax income fell 3.5% y/y as interest expense nearly tripled to $201M from $71M and Corporate other expense rose to $353M from $277M, per the segment-information table.
Net income fell 16.4% y/y on the pretax decline above plus a higher income tax expense of $321M versus $203M a year earlier.

GAAP diluted EPS fell 15.9% y/y on the net-income decline; the company's own reconciliation shows $0.49 acquisition/divestiture charges, $0.05 restructuring, and $0.50 intangible amortization per share excluded from adjusted EPS, which itself rose to a Q2 record $3.15.
Mirrors the diluted EPS move above on the same net-income decline against a comparable basic share count (388.5M vs 390.3M y/y).
Long-term debt rose 87.4% y/y, consistent with debt-financed acquisitions disclosed in Note 3: Boyd Thermal ($9.55B, closed March 2026) and Ultra PCS ($1.53B, closed January 2026).
Short-term borrowings rose 88.2% y/y alongside the long-term debt increase above, both consistent with financing for the Boyd Thermal and Ultra PCS acquisitions disclosed in Note 3.
Not explained in the release beyond the general cash flow statement; cash fell q/q but is up y/y.
Not explained in the release; equity growth is consistent with retained net income accumulation over the trailing year.
